title: Entangling Atomic Quantum Memories Using High-Order Modulated Coherent States
authors: Chaohan Cui, Prajit Dhara, Saikat Guha
abstract: High-order coherent-state modulation with reflective cavity-coupled atomic memories can distribute multiple heralded ebits per transmitted optical mode, but requires a collective midpoint POVM optimized for maximum distillable entanglement rather than minimum-error state discrimination. An SRM-inspired 16-QAM receiver reaches $1.75$ ebits per mode at $0.5$~dB end-to-end loss, $3.8$~dB below the half-link capacity benchmark. For 4-QAM, a variational POVM with more outcomes than constellation points improves the SRM rate by $4.0\%$ yet remains below capacity, revealing measurement-design headroom. The advantage over single-qubit-per-mode midpoint protocols persists for per-interface loss $<0.2$~dB and calibrated phase error $<0.2π$.
summary: This work proposes using high-order Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) on optical modes to significantly boost the rate of entanglement distribution between quantum memories. By optimizing the measurement scheme (POVM), the authors demonstrate that this approach surpasses conventional single-qubit protocols, paving the way for scalable quantum networking architectures.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of distributing high-rate, high-fidelity entanglement between distant quantum memories using optical interconnects.
main_result: A high-order M-QAM modulation scheme, implemented with an SRM-inspired receiver, can distribute multiqubit entanglement, achieving rates significantly higher than single-qubit-per-mode protocols.
method: The authors model the entanglement distribution using a collective midpoint POVM optimized for distillable entanglement, comparing the achievable rate against theoretical capacity bounds.
model_or_system: The system involves reflective cavity-coupled atomic quantum memories (Alice and Bob) communicating via optical modes to a central receiver (Charlie). The protocol maps a q-qubit register onto an M=2^q QAM alphabet.
key_observables: Distillable entanglement rate (ebits/mode), achievable rate vs. loss, and the improvement factor over single-photon baselines.
important_parameters: End-to-end channel loss (L_ch), QAM order (M=2^q), and systematic conditional-phase error ($\delta\phi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on constructing an explicit achievable receiver (SRM-inspired) and assumes the use of a strongly coupled reflective-cavity qubit–photon interface.
figures_summary: Figures compare entanglement generation rates across different modulation orders and losses, illustrate the optimization of QAM spacing versus loss, and compare the performance of different receiver designs (SRM vs. variational POVM).
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the physical setup and the entanglement objective (maximizing distillable entanglement) to developing the mathematical framework using M-QAM states, deriving the achievable rate via the SRM-inspired POVM, and finally comparing this rate against theoretical benchmarks and alternative measurement strategies.
why_interesting: It provides concrete, quantitative results on scaling entanglement distribution beyond simple single-photon protocols by leveraging high-dimensional coherent state modulation, which is crucial for scaling quantum networks.
